fills.notes: The clause contrasts the letter-form with its total content: the answer-letter ‘did not lack’ any report. This fits the substrate’s impersonal, exhaustive ‘tidings’ register and avoids later moralizing.

After ‘in the answer that the First Man …’ the syntax demands a verb of inscription/reporting parallel to ‘in which all the tidings are written down’. ‘Set down’ preserves the correspondential sense: the inner states (wars/contests) are fixed into a stable form (letter).
Retained: it matches the fixed triad ‘what has happened / what will happen / what is prepared to be done’, the substrate’s comprehensive foreknowledge schema.

assessment: Most of the damage can be restored by tight parallelism: both summons and answer are ‘letters’ containing the total account of past and future effects. Exact verb choices remain somewhat open, but the required sense (no omission; complete inscription) is strongly constrained by the correspondential structure.
